title: LLM cost, metering, keys and caching

questions.text: Through which single client does this paid call go, and does it emit one raw-unit usage event per attempt?
What is the worst-case cost of one trigger with the largest allowed input? Show the arithmetic.
What stops it: per-job ceiling, per-tenant quota, kill switch? What does each do on error? (It must deny.)
Who pays (BYOK, gateway or system key), and how will I see that from the response, not from config?
Which model, and which eval shows a cheaper one is not good enough? Can it run batched?
What event triggers the call, and what predicate skips it? Have we computed this result before (cache key, TTL, negative cache)?
Is the prompt prefix stable and over the model's minimum cacheable length? Where is the breakpoint, and what changes before it?
Where do limits come from at decision time (source of truth or a cache), and how stale can they be?
For experiments: sample size from a power analysis, cost estimate, budget, stop rule. For keys: ledger state checked before testing?

budgets.measure: worst-case arithmetic in pre-flight + metered sum per job
bypass scan (cost.direct-sdk) outside the metered client
budgets.source: design by contract: single choke point

budgets.measure: metered sum vs provider usage export per provider per day

rules.title: Provider SDK used directly outside the metered client
rules.why: Every call here is spend nobody records or bills.
rules.confirm: failing-test: mock the provider, call the path, assert one usage event per attempt (fails: zero)
rules.fixHint: route through the project's metered client; set metered paths in .jstack/unslop.json extraRules if they differ

rules.title: Quota/spend gate that allows on error (catch returns true/null)
rules.why: When the quota store is down, every paid call goes through (CWE-636).
rules.confirm: failing-test: make the quota store throw; assert the paid call is not made
rules.fixHint: deny on error for paid actions; document any degrade mode

rules.title: Gate defaults to allow (?? true / || true)
rules.why: A missing limit reads as unlimited.
rules.confirm: failing-test: limit row absent; assert denied

rules.title: Per-item paid call in a loop with no size bound or job ceiling before it
rules.why: A big upload (or a zip bomb) multiplies the bill.
rules.confirm: failing-test: 10k-entry archive through the entry point with the provider mocked; calls before rejection > N

rules.title: Message or webhook handler calls the model on every event
rules.confirm: failing-test: replay a chat log; paid calls > messages meeting the trigger

rules.title: Timestamp, id or user name before the cache breakpoint; tools in non-deterministic order
rules.why: Every request misses the prompt cache.
rules.confirm: measurement: cache hit ratio per call site near 0; prompt prefix diff across two users

rules.title: Usage logged as converted credits or dollars instead of raw provider units
rules.why: Pricing changes cannot be replayed; reconciliation with the invoice breaks.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the usage event has no input/output token fields

rules.title: One spend or rate pool shared by several agents or users with no per-consumer cap
rules.why: One busy consumer spends the pool and every other one is refused.
rules.confirm: failing-test: consumer A loops until the pool is spent; consumer B is refused

rules.title: Quota or plan limit read from the session, token claims or a long-lived cache at decision time
rules.why: A raised or lowered limit takes effect only after re-login, so users are blocked or overspend.
rules.confirm: failing-test: raise the limit in the store; the next request is still refused until re-login

verify.text: bypass scan clean (scan.mjs cost.direct-sdk / ESLint no-restricted-imports)

quota store down -> paid call refused; bad BYOK key -> system-credit fallback visible and alerted

cache hit ratio per call site from usage fields; prompt prefix diff across two users
metered sum vs provider usage export per provider per day within budget
